description: Baseline AES-256-GCM RTL wired to the autonomous harness. This file records how the repository currently executes the experiment; experiment.json remains the frozen contract.

criteria.criterion: normative AES and GCM revisions are pinned
criteria.note: Recorded in experiments/aes-256-gcm/PROFILE.md. No executable check can establish that a document names the right revision, so this stays a reviewed criterion rather than an automated pass.

criteria.criterion: byte/bit order, IV, tag, length, reset, and tag-failure semantics are documented
criteria.note: PROFILE.md states each decision; the edge-case and negative workloads exercise them, but the documentation itself is reviewed by a human.

criteria.criterion: target profile and objective function are explicit
criteria.note: No physical target is frozen yet. This criterion is deliberately unevaluated rather than assumed.

criteria.criterion: primitive, full-GCM, edge, random, and interface workloads pass
synthesizable RTL lint and synthesis pass
candidate never calls host crypto or reads oracle verdicts
cycle and throughput measurements are reproducible for frozen vectors
all unknown metrics and security limitations are labeled
criteria.note: Area is measured in generic Yosys cells only; no target library, timing, or power number exists, and the run record carries those as null. A human confirms the labelling is honest.

criteria.criterion: named FPGA or ASIC target accepts the exact RTL configuration
criteria.note: No FPGA or ASIC flow is installed on this host. lab/status reports the capability as unavailable.

criteria.criterion: timing constraints and resource reports are retained
physical output matches RTL for the same vectors
each security claim has a stated threat model
criteria.note: PROFILE.md states the threat model and the claim boundary.

criteria.criterion: data-dependent control and latency paths are inspected or asserted
physical leakage/fault claims use appropriate measurements rather than simulation-only inference
criteria.note: No leakage instrumentation exists here. Simulation cannot establish this, so it must never be marked passed from RTL evidence.
